Project Description:
The area under Sundarban Tiger Reserve is proposed to be  increased by inclusion of  the Tiger bearing areas of 24 Parganas South Division within the tiger reserve.
The population of tigers in the mangrove forest areas of the  adjacent 24 Parganas South Division has been increasing for the past 2 decades. The area needs greater degree of protection in order to ensure the conservation of tigers in the Sundarban Region.  

The Current jurisdiction of Sundarban Tiger Reserve is 259173 ha and the jurisidiction of 24 Parganas South Division is 104468 ha. As per the proposal the area after the reorganisation will be 363641 ha.  
The proposal for the inclusion of the areas have been approved in principal by the State Government and National Tiger Conservation Authority. The proposal is now being placed before the National Board For Wildlife for the approval. Since the agenda points for NBWL is taken only through the Parivesh portal, the proposal is hereby sent through the portal.
Project Name: Reorganisation of Sundarban Tiger Reserve

Project Description:
BRIEF BACKGROUND DIVERSION OF 1400 ACRES RETHIKHOLA FOREST LAND

1.  Govt of India, Ministry of Defence in the year 1971 vide GSL No 55/56/Q3(H)/149-S/D(Q&C) dt 03 May 1971 accorded diversion of 1400 acres of Forest land at Rethikhola Range to Army.

2.  Out of 1400 acres, 1118.73 acres Forest land was handed over to Army from 1971 to 1976 in piecemeal as under:-

	(a)	 40.51 Acres in 21 May 1966.

	(b)	167.00 acres in 02 Dec 1971.

	(c)	398.22 acres in 12 Feb 1973.

	(d)	95.00 acres in 03 May 1975.

Project Description: The Upper Neora Small Hydro Project is a proposed 6 MW run-of-river type hydroelectric development located on the Neora River, a perennial mountain stream originating in the Rechila Hill Reserve Forest within the Neora Valley National Park in the Darjeeling Himalayas. The river, which flows south through Kalimpong before joining the Chel River, is fed by nine principal tributaries and sixteen minor streams, ensuring a reliable flow regime year-round. This project is strategically located upstream of the Lower Neora Small Hydro Project (SHP) and is designed to optimally harness the available head and discharge in the upper reaches of the Neora River basin.The Project is designed as a 6 MW run-of-river scheme, beginning with a trench-type weir at El. 452.30 m that diverts discharge of 12.90 m³/sec of water through intake well. From there, the flow is directed to a 2.5 m dia. feeder channel of 289 m length to connect two nos. conventional rectangular desilting chamber.
